question: In skeletal skeletal muscle of mammals:

options.opa: A motor neuron supplies all its fibers.
options.opb: Each motor neuron supplies a single fiber.
options.opc: Each fiber receives innervation from a single motor neuron.
options.opd: Summation of synaptic potentials is required to reach the excitation threshold.

analysis: In mammalian skeletal muscle, each muscle fiber is typically innervated by a single motor neuron, which forms a neuromuscular junction. This ensures precise control of muscle contraction. Therefore, option opc is correct. While a motor neuron can innervate multiple muscle fibers, each fiber receives input from only one motor neuron. Summation of synaptic potentials is not required at the neuromuscular junction because the release of acetylcholine from the motor neuron is usually sufficient to reach the excitation threshold of the muscle fiber.
